blocks.html: The scatter diagram (recall §4.4) showed that older children in the under-five clinic tend to weigh more. This chapter turns that picture into numbers. It defines covariance and Pearson’s r with their test and confidence interval (§11.2), the rank-based coefficients of Spearman and Kendall (§11.3) and the coefficients for binary variables (§11.4). It then asks what an association can and cannot tell you about cause (§11.5), builds the idea of confounding and draws it with causal diagrams (§11.6), and closes with the first method that removes a confounder’s distortion: stratified analysis with the Mantel–Haenszel estimators (§11.7).
